verdict: S&P Global grew revenue 7% to $3.7B and continuing-operations EPS jumped 26%, helped by a $200M gain on a disposition in Energy — while Indices surged 20% and the company put Capital IQ under strategic review after spinning off Mobility.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: vs a year ago, from continuing operations

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: continuing operations, vs $3.54 a year ago; $4.25 including the discontinued Mobility loss

kpis.label: Share repurchases
kpis.note: bought back in the quarter; more than $4B year to date

segments.name: Market Intelligence
segments.note: Data, research and analytics subscriptions for investors and companies — the largest division, and home to Capital IQ, which is now under strategic review.

segments.name: Ratings
segments.note: Fees for rating bonds and loans — the joint-largest division this quarter, growing slowly after a strong first half.

segments.name: Energy
segments.note: Commodity price assessments and energy data (the business formerly called Commodity Insights), including a $200M gain on a disposition booked below revenue in expenses.

segments.name: Indices
segments.note: Licensing stock and bond indexes such as the S&P 500 to funds and trading products — the fastest-growing division, up 20%.

segments.name: Intersegment eliminations
segments.note: Sales between the company's own divisions, removed so revenue is not counted twice.

opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: All of the company's running costs across its four divisions, net of a $200M gain on a disposition in Energy that reduced reported expenses. Deal-related amortization of acquired intangibles was $199M of the total.

otherDetail: Net other expense of $83M is $87M of net interest expense partly offset by $4M of other income.
footerNote: Net income of $1,240M is the amount attributable to S&P Global shareholders: $1,406M earned from continuing operations, minus a $58M loss from the discontinued Mobility business (spun off on July 1, 2026) and $108M attributable to noncontrolling interests. Mobility is excluded from revenue throughout, so the divisions shown are the four continuing ones — Ratings, Indices, Energy (formerly Commodity Insights) and Market Intelligence.

takeaways.title: Indices is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Indices revenue rose 20% to $554M as demand for benchmarks and the products built on them kept climbing — it drove a large share of the quarter's $235M revenue increase.

takeaways.title: A one-off gain flatters profit
takeaways.text: A $200M gain on a disposition in Energy lifted GAAP operating profit 26% to $1,956M. On an adjusted basis, operating profit grew 8% — still solid, but not the headline jump.

takeaways.title: A leaner company after the spin-off
takeaways.text: With Mobility spun off on July 1 and Capital IQ now under strategic review, S&P Global is narrowing itself around ratings, benchmarks and data — continuing EPS of $4.45 rose 26% on profit growth and buybacks.

oneTimers: $200M gain on a disposition in the Energy segment, which lifted GAAP operating profit; adjusted results exclude it.

Mobility was spun off on July 1, 2026 and is treated as discontinued operations (a $58M loss in the quarter); S&P Global also announced a strategic review of Capital IQ and associated data businesses within Market Intelligence.
